screens.name: Home — current Chrome/WebKit, 390/430, normal/200%, populated omen
screens.evidence: Sheets 23–24 and 55–56 show consistent current layouts, and supplied browser evidence reports complete omens, balanced navigation, contrast passes and no collisions.
findings: Strengthen the small normal-size 'Touch the ball' instruction so the dominant decorative orb also has an immediately apparent action.

screens.name: Home — unavailable omen
screens.evidence: Sheet 25 shows 'Unavailable today' and 'Return tomorrow' beneath a usable-looking primary orb in normal, transition and large-text views.
findings: Clarify whether the omen is intentionally unavailable for the day or temporarily failed so 'Return tomorrow' feels justified.

screens.name: Home — omen loading and populated fixture
screens.evidence: Sheets 25 and 54 show the populated fixture and 'A little starlight is finding you...' at both text sizes.
findings: Pair the poetic loading line with a brief explicit loading label to distinguish pending content from the omen itself.

screens.name: Approach
screens.evidence: Sheet 01 preserves the orb and invitation across transition and settled views but shows only 'You can speak or type next' as guidance.
findings: Make the next step or automatic progression explicit because the invitation does not identify an actionable control.

screens.name: Ask — myself, focused question
screens.evidence: Sheets 01 and 03 show labeled focused input and a dominant submit action, supported by supplied draft-retention and focus checks.
findings: Shorten the disclosure visually while preserving its meaning so the question remains the strongest content at 200%.

screens.name: Ask — named person, collapsed composer
screens.evidence: Sheets 02 and 43 show 'About Alex · change', the complete question and primary and voice actions at normal and enlarged sizes.
findings: Separate the recipient name from the change affordance more clearly to make the editable context quicker to scan.

screens.name: Ask — person selection and first-name input
screens.evidence: Sheets 02–03 show a checked Someone option, labeled Alex input, privacy explanation and confirmation, with cancellation visible in normal views.
findings: Use the same rounded input and focus treatment as the question composer to remove the conspicuous rectangular styling change.

screens.name: Ask — explicit AI consent pending
screens.evidence: Sheet 13 shows an off consent switch and disabled submit in a constrained viewport, while supplied evidence reports zero requests before opt-in.
findings: Keep a concise explanation of the required consent beside the disabled submit when the full disclosure is scrolled away.

screens.name: Ask — constrained typing and long question
screens.evidence: Sheet 20 shows labeled input and submit together in the 500px viewport, and supplied tests report complete 500-character retention and disclosure retrieval.
findings: Provide a subtle internal-scroll cue for long drafts so partial first and last lines do not suggest lost text.

screens.name: Ask — disclosure retrieved in constrained viewport
screens.evidence: Sheet 20 shows the recipient and complete disclosure retrieved above the question field within the letterboxed constrained viewport.
findings: Maintain a clear route back to the active field after reviewing the disclosure without requiring users to rediscover its position.

screens.name: Listening — microphone could not start
screens.evidence: Sheet 26 shows a clear failure explanation, dominant typing fallback and secondary voice retry across normal, transition and large states.
findings: Place the microphone failure message closer to the heading at normal size to reduce the gap before the recovery action.

screens.name: Planning — loading
screens.evidence: Sheet 41 identifies question checking, an up-to-one-minute wait, credit protection and cancellation, with decorative art removed in large text.
findings: Keep the stage description prominent enough to distinguish this wait from the later forecast-generation wait.

screens.name: Research — loading
screens.evidence: Sheet 45 shows current-context research copy, cancellation and credit protection with stable transition-to-settled composition.
findings: Reduce the high-contrast mist around the normal-size orb slightly so progress information receives more attention.

screens.name: Adaptive card 1 — plan readiness
screens.evidence: Sheets 07–08 show the complete question, four choices and '1 of 3', with the orb omitted at large text.
findings: Reduce the normal-size gap between orb and question to make the task begin sooner without weakening the hero.

screens.name: Adaptive card 2 — obstacle
screens.evidence: Sheet 08 shows Time, Money, Nerve and free-text choices with consistent normal and transition layouts and a large-text alternative.
findings: Make the choice rows slightly more visibly interactive before selection while preserving their borderless treatment.

screens.name: Adaptive card 3 — support
screens.evidence: Sheet 09 shows '3 of 3' and explicitly changes the instruction to 'Choose an answer to reveal'.
findings: Preserve this explicit final-step consequence and add equivalent clarity to earlier auto-advancing choices.

screens.name: Custom answer — empty
screens.evidence: Sheets 09–10 show the original question, labeled empty answer, disabled Continue and a reason for the disabled state.
findings: Unify the square answer field with the rounded composer field so the same kind of text entry feels consistent.

screens.name: Custom answer — populated and constrained long answer
screens.evidence: Sheets 19–20 retain question context and Reveal within constrained layouts, while the unconstrained populated state still says to write a few words.
findings: Remove or update 'Write a few words to continue' once a valid answer is present.

screens.name: Opening — ordinary charge, separation and settle
screens.evidence: Sheets 33–35 depict the opening sequence, and supplied evidence reports saved-once integrity, immediate keyboard skip and an isolated near-60fps trace.
findings: Refine the broad black separation wedge so the release reads as intentional glass movement rather than a missing slice of the orb.

screens.name: Opening — golden variation
screens.evidence: Sheets 31–33 show the warmer ring and golden settled label, with supplied timing and frame measurements for the controlled opening.
findings: Keep the golden distinction restrained but make its visible release more coherent than the current dark central split.

screens.name: Opening — reduced motion, system reduce and skip
screens.evidence: Sheets 35–36 show matching settled outcomes, and supplied browser tests report a calm crossfade without transforms or particles and immediate skip.
findings: Retain the identical result hierarchy across reduced-motion and skipped openings.

screens.name: Opening — interruption and early Share return
screens.evidence: Sheets 31 and 33 show the early-share and interrupted settled states, supported by reported persistence and no-replay keyboard-path checks.
findings: Carry a brief saved-reading confirmation through interruption so the successful preservation is apparent to users as well as tests.

screens.name: Reveal — settled forecast
screens.evidence: Sheets 46–47 show the speculative label, forecast, reminder and actions in normal and large text with a consistent settled arrangement.
findings: Give the forecast more visual priority relative to the prominent Share button and the stack of follow-up actions.

screens.name: Check-in — initial, forecast collapsed
screens.evidence: Sheets 11 and 37 preserve the original question, collapsed forecast, three outcomes and reminder context at normal and large text.
findings: Reduce the visual competition from sharing and editing so recording an outcome remains the unmistakable primary task.

screens.name: Check-in — forecast expanded
screens.evidence: Sheets 10–11 and 36 show the expanded forecast above outcomes, with supplied keyboard disclosure checks and enlarged-text coverage.
findings: Make the outcome section easier to return to after expansion, which pushes it well down the large-text view.

screens.name: Check-in — Came true saved
screens.evidence: Sheet 39 shows both a Saved message and checked Came true row, and supplied evidence reports persisted selection with unchanged reminder date.
findings: Keep the redundant text-and-check confirmation while reducing the prominence of unrelated actions below it.

screens.name: Check-in — Did not happen saved
screens.evidence: Sheets 37–38 show explicit saved failure outcomes at both text sizes, supported by reported correction and persistence checks.
findings: Preserve the neutral treatment of negative outcomes and keep changing the answer visibly available.

screens.name: Check-in — Still waiting saved
screens.evidence: Sheets 37–38 show checked Still waiting, saved status and an explicit statement that the reminder date stays unchanged.
findings: Retain the clear distinction between a pending outcome and a completed check-in.

screens.name: Evidence — overview
screens.evidence: Sheets 43 and 45–46 show four clearly separated evidence destinations with descriptions and a large-text list.
findings: Consolidate 'Back to forecast' and 'Read the forecast' or make their different destinations explicit.

screens.name: Evidence — why this forecast, direct and reader variants
screens.evidence: Sheets 16–17, 44 and 47 show preserved legacy prose in numbered passages, with visible heading focus and reported keyboard-return checks.
findings: Add a concise summary of the scenario's basis and limits before the long preserved passages.

screens.name: Evidence — answers, question-labeled and legacy numbered
screens.evidence: Sheets 15 and 42 show long preserved answers, with full question labels in one variant and generic Answer labels in the legacy reader.
findings: Use the original question as each answer's heading whenever that context is available.

screens.name: Evidence — assumptions
screens.evidence: Sheets 15–16 and 42 show a distinct Assumptions title, speculative qualifier and preserved long content at both sizes.
findings: Present discrete assumption units where the underlying content supports them to improve scanning without truncation.

screens.name: Evidence — current sources
screens.evidence: Sheets 17 and 44 distinguish source publisher, date, long description and external link while explicitly limiting sources to background context.
findings: Move or repeat the source-opening action beside the publisher so long descriptions do not delay access to the source.

screens.name: Share — preview and download
screens.evidence: Sheets 50 and 52 show a compact card preview, image-text route, enlargement and dominant Download image action.
findings: Increase the useful preview size at large text or prioritize its text alternative so the preview remains informative.

screens.name: Share — invite and remind options expanded
screens.evidence: Sheet 51 shows the expanded Invite & remind section below privacy copy and the download action, with the header occluding scrolled title content.
findings: Make the secondary section's expanded state clearer and reduce the amount of repeated content users must pass to reach it.

screens.name: Share — full image inspection / story
screens.evidence: Sheets 50 and 53–54 show the larger export card with forecast, speculative warning, branding and a back-to-sharing action.
findings: Keep the image-text alternative directly discoverable from the inspection view for users who cannot comfortably read bitmap text.

screens.name: Share — image text
screens.evidence: Sheets 51–52 expose the forecast, qualifier and branding as scalable text above Download image and the visual preview.
findings: Add a little separation between Download image and the repeated preview to avoid the two surfaces appearing attached.

screens.name: Export — preparing
screens.evidence: Sheet 18 shows disabled download with 'Preparing image...', and supplied held-encoding checks report single-flight behavior at both sizes.
findings: Preserve the status directly beside the disabled action throughout any scrolling or text-size change.

screens.name: Export — download started
screens.evidence: Sheet 18 reports 'Image download started' rather than claiming device storage, and supplied evidence includes a real encoded PNG download.
findings: Retain the precise started wording and avoid duplicating the privacy reassurance immediately beneath it.

screens.name: Export — failure and retry
screens.evidence: Sheet 19 shows 'Try download again' with a plain failure message, supported by reported forced-failure and successful retry checks.
findings: Keep the failure message adjacent to retry and preserve the preview during recovery.

screens.name: History — empty
screens.evidence: Sheets 21–22 show the local-storage note, centered empty-state invitation and Ask the Ball route at both sizes.

screens.name: History — populated single and stress list
screens.evidence: Sheets 21–22 show dates, original questions, forecasts, reminders and check-in links, with multiple records separated by rules.

screens.name: History — persisted outcome
screens.evidence: Sheet 22 shows a checked Came true result within the first history record, supported by supplied persistence checks.

screens.name: Sky — offline sample stars and selected question

screens.name: Circles — offline

screens.name: Onboarding — age confirmation
screens.evidence: Sheets 26–27 show the age question, no-birthday explanation and explicit older/under-13 actions at normal and large sizes.

screens.name: Onboarding — optional birthday

screens.name: Onboarding — age blocked

screens.name: Onboarding — focus unselected

limitations: Scores are provisional browser assessments using the attached screenshots and supplied runtime report; no independent live interaction was performed.
A is the mean of hierarchy, typography and surfaces; F is the mean of clarity, feedback and accessibility; overall is 0.4A + 0.6F, rounded to one decimal, excluding genuinely inapplicable dimensions.
The authorized A>=9 and F>=9 threshold is not met for every screen or meaningful component.
No confirmed hard-gate failure is established by this evidence; offscreen content in a scrollable capture alone does not prove an unreachable action.
Several scrolled views show content occluded at fixed viewport boundaries; screenshots cannot establish whether every focused control is fully revealed during actual navigation.

Transition screenshots support visual continuity but cannot independently establish frame pacing, announcement timing or the complete motion experience; supplied measurements inform those provisional scores.
Physical iPhone Safari, native Dynamic Type, VoiceOver, actual keyboard, microphone, haptics, payments and OS sharing remain unverified and are not certified by browser results.
Axe, target-size and contrast checks do not establish complete assistive-technology usability or novice task success.
Circles is represented only offline; populated circles, invitations, production authentication and eligibility behavior cannot be evaluated.
Controlled predictions, long stress content and historical confidence wording are fixtures; they do not establish predictive accuracy, source quality or calibrated confidence.
The 500px constrained captures are synthetic viewport checks, and their surrounding letterboxing is not app layout.
No repeated novice study or independently inspected full interaction recording was supplied, so exemplary end-to-end outcomes are not established.
topFixes: Clarify the Approach next step and keep consent requirements visible beside disabled submission in constrained views.
Refine the opening's dark separation wedge so the orb release looks intentional and materially coherent.
Unify input shapes and focus styling; remove stale empty-answer guidance after valid text is entered.
Strengthen forecast and check-in task hierarchy relative to sharing, editing and other secondary actions.
Polish enlarged-text spacing, fixed-header scroll boundaries and long-input scroll cues without reducing text scaling.
Simplify repeated Circles and sharing copy, and distinguish disclosure expansion from navigation consistently.
Complete physical-device and assistive-technology checks after browser refinements; retain the provisional boundary until those results exist.
